links.outcome: Emergency under-triage rate on clinician-authored triage vignettes
links.effect: OpenEvidence under-triaged 12.5% of emergency presentations versus 51.6% in the previously reported ChatGPT Health benchmark; objective data eliminated emergency under-triage (25% to 0%; p = 0.005).
links.quote: OpenEvidence under-triaged 12.5 % of emergency presentations versus 51.6 % in the previously reported ChatGPT Health benchmark, and over-triaged 68.0 % of nonurgent Home presentations (ChatGPT Health, 64.8 %).

links.outcome: Missed emergencies and unnecessary escalation (over-triage) in AI triage recommendations
links.effect: Emergency under-triage 12.5%; over-triage of 68.0% of nonurgent Home presentations; clear-case accuracy 71.3%.
links.quote: OpenEvidence under-triaged 12.5 % of emergency presentations versus 51.6 % in the previously reported ChatGPT Health benchmark, and over-triaged 68.0 % of nonurgent Home presentations (ChatGPT Health, 64.8 %).

links.outcome: Change in triage recommendations when demographic and contextual modifiers varied in prompts
links.effect: Anchoring statements did not alter recommendations (OR = 1.08, 95% CI 0.62-1.88; Holm-adjusted p = 1.0).
links.quote: Anchoring statements did not alter recommendations (OR = 1.08, 95 % CI 0.62-1.88; Holm-adjusted p = 1.0).

links.outcome: Rate of declining to assign a triage level (deferral/refusal) on symptom-only prompts
links.effect: Platform declined to assign a triage level in 65 of 960 responses (6.8%), exclusively in symptom-only Home or Routine prompts.
links.quote: In 65 of 960 responses (6.8 %), the platform declined to assign a triage level, exclusively in symptom-only Home or Routine prompts.

unlisted_practices: Treating evidence-seeking refusal as a distinct output category in evaluation
Providing objective clinical data in prompts to improve triage accuracy
Testing susceptibility to social anchoring statements in triage prompts

screen.reason: The study evaluates the triage safety profile and performance of OpenEvidence (an LLM-based clinical decision support tool) using 960 simulated vignette prompts, benchmarking accuracy and refusal behavior.
